newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk opposition plans government censure Friday.
newsitem.headline: Turk opposition plans government censure Friday.

text.p: Turkish conservative leader Mesut Yilmaz said on Thursday opposition MPs were aiming to submit a censure motion by the weekend to try to topple the Islamist-conservative coalition.

"We are planning to submit the censure motion by tomorrow evening," the state-run Anatolian news agency quoted Yilmaz as saying. "Our aim is to ensure the censure motion is discussed in parliament next week."
Opposition and dissident government MPs have been negotiating for some time to try to bring down the government led by Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
Turkish stocks rallied strongly on hopes that a new secularist government was on the horizon, ending at 1,515, or 5.43 percent up on Wednesday's close.
The market was particularly optimistic that a new government might be formed without a laborious election and inter-party negotiation process.

But the anti-Islamist efforts suffered a possible setback because of a decision by the junior coalition partner to discipline leading rebel government MP Yalim Erez over his role in the anti-government move.
"The party executive only has the authority to form a government or withdraw from it," Huseyin Uyanik, a senior MP for Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller's True Path Party (DYP), told reporters.
"We have been reviewing Mugla MP Yalim Erez's negotiations," he said. "The discipline mechanism has been set in motion."
The DYP executive council met on Thursday at 3.30 p.m. to discuss the latest political developments.
Erez had asked for an appointment with Ciller to discuss withdrawing from the government, but she has not yet accepted his request.
Yilmaz suggested the censure motion would be submitted regardless of whether or not Ciller agreed to talks.
"We are awaiting several things, that is one of them, but we will probably submit the censure motion tomorrow," he said.

But the DYP move against Erez could result in his sacking from the party, which could put off other MPs he says will join an alternative government against Erbakan's Welfare Party's alliance with the DYP.
Uyanik said Erez had been asked to submit a written explanation of his actions by Tuesday.
Erbakan and Ciller formed a coalition in June, making Erbakan modern Turkey's first Islamist leader.

But the government has been under pressure from the strongly secularist army over religious activism, and the partners have been divided over the implementation of military-led demands to curb Islamist zeal.
